hpi_details: 30M presents with a painful, shallow ulcer on the shaft of his penis for 3 days. It started as small blisters. He also complains of a low-grade fever and painful swollen glands in his groin. He has a new sexual partner.
concerns: worried it will never go away
social_hx: Sexually active with a new partner, inconsistent condom use

core_concepts: Primary outbreak often features painful vesicles/ulcers, tender lymphadenopathy, and systemic symptoms (fever, malaise).
common_misconceptions: Assuming a painless ulcer is herpes (syphilis is painless, herpes is painful).
dangerous_errors: Failing to screen for other STIs (HIV, Syphilis, GC/CT) when a patient presents with one STI.
management_principles: Oral antivirals (Valacyclovir/Acyclovir), STI screening, counseling on transmission.
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

source_refs.title: Infectious Diseases Society of America (IDSA) Clinical Practice Guidelines

reference_soap.subjective: 30M with a painful genital ulcer, fever, and tender groin lumps.
reference_soap.objective: Multiple shallow, painful, erythematous based ulcers on penile shaft. Bilateral tender inguinal lymphadenopathy.
reference_soap.assessment: Primary Genital Herpes Simplex Virus (HSV) infection.
reference_soap.plan: HSV PCR swab. Start oral Valacyclovir. Full STI screening (HIV, Syphilis, Gonorrhea, Chlamydia).

learning_objectives: Differentiate painful genital ulcers (herpes, chancroid) from painless (syphilis).

teaching.one_liner: Painful genital vesicles and ulcers with tender inguinal lymphadenopathy typical of primary HSV infection.
red_flags: Urinary retention (due to severe pain or radiculopathy)

must_ask.say: Did the sore start as small blisters before it became an ulcer?
Have you noticed any swollen, tender glands in your groin?
Have you had a fever or felt generally unwell?
Have you had any new sexual partners recently, and do you use protection?

history.answer: I came in because I have painful sores on my penis that started a few days ago.
They started 3 days ago. At first, they looked like tiny blisters, and then they popped and turned into open sores.
Yes, they started out as small, clustered water blisters before breaking open into sores.
The sores are right on the shaft of my penis. They haven't spread anywhere else on my body.
It's a burning, stinging pain, especially when anything rubs against it. I would rate it around 6 out of 10.
Wearing tight pants or underwear rubs against them and hurts worse, and taking a warm shower stings. Nothing really relieves it.
Yes, about 2 days ago I noticed tender, swollen lumps on both sides of my groin.
I've been feeling slightly feverish and fatigued with mild body aches since yesterday.
It stings a bit when urine touches the open sores, but I can pee normally and my bladder empties completely.
No, there is no pus or liquid leaking from the tip of my penis.
No, I don't have any sores in my mouth, around my anus, or anywhere else.
No vision problems, no joint pain, and no weakness or numbness in my legs.
No, my weight has been completely steady and I haven't had night sweats.
No, I have never had sores, blisters, or anything like this before. This is the very first time.
I tried washing the area with soap and putting on some petroleum jelly, but it didn't help at all.
I am sexually active and started seeing a new partner about a week ago.
We used condoms once or twice, but we didn't use them consistently every time.
She didn't mention having any sores or symptoms, and I didn't see anything unusual on her.
It's uncomfortable to walk, and wearing underwear is painful enough that it keeps waking me up at night.
I'm really worried that I caught a sexually transmitted infection from my new partner.
I'm terrified that this might be something permanent that will never go away.
I was hoping you could give me some antibiotics to clear this infection up quickly.
I don't have any chronic medical conditions like diabetes or high blood pressure.
I've never had any surgeries and I've never been admitted to a hospital.
I am not taking any prescription drugs, over-the-counter medications, or herbal supplements.
I don't have any known allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I don't smoke cigarettes, vape, or use any recreational drugs.
I drink one or two beers on the weekend when hanging out with friends, but that's all.
I work as an IT technician in an office, and I live alone in an apartment.
My parents and siblings are all healthy, with no major health problems that I know of.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 120/80 mmHg, heart rate 78 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, body temperature 37.8 C, oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Alert, oriented, in mild discomfort when moving or sitting, with no acute respiratory distress.
Oral mucosa and posterior pharynx are pink and clear with no aphthous ulcers or lesions.
Abdomen is soft, flat, and non-tender, with no suprapubic tenderness or palpable bladder distension.
Multiple shallow, painful ulcers with erythematous bases on the mid-shaft of the penis, with no urethral discharge.
Bilateral tender, enlarged, mobile inguinal lymph nodes without overlying erythema or fluctuance.
No generalized rash, and palms and soles are clear without maculopapular lesions.
